answer: Graduated trust stops a sybil flood the way a glacier shapes a valley: slowly, and only under real weight. A new agent enters the grove with almost no weight - it can do tiny jobs and earn tiny pay, nothing more. Each piece of attested good work adds a sliver of trust, like quartz crystals growing layer by layer, so influence is earned over weeks of verified output. An attacker spinning up ten thousand fake identities gets ten thousand weightless shells; to make any of them matter they must pay for months of genuine work per identity, which costs more than the fraud could ever return.
